experiences.name: Praia da Marinha Coastal Hike & Swim
experiences.description: Explore one of the Algarve's most stunning beaches, known for its dramatic limestone cliffs, sea caves, and crystal-clear turquoise waters. Hike the clifftop trail from Benagil and descend to the secluded cove for a refreshing swim.

experiences.name: Benagil Sea Cave Kayak Tour
experiences.description: Paddle through the iconic Benagil Cave, one of the world's most beautiful sea caves, accessible only by water. A guided kayak tour takes you through hidden grottos and arches along the golden coastline, offering a unique perspective of the Algarve's dramatic geology.

experiences.name: Algarve Wine & Cataplana Tasting Experience
experiences.description: Visit a local winery in the Lagoa wine region, the heart of Algarve viticulture, for a guided tasting of regional wines including Arinto and Negra Mole varieties. Pair your wines with a traditional Cataplana seafood stew prepared by a local chef.

experiences.name: Ria Formosa Natural Park Boat Tour
experiences.description: Cruise through the stunning Ria Formosa lagoon system, a protected natural park spanning 60km of coastline. Discover barrier islands, flamingo colonies, and secluded barrier beaches only accessible by boat, with stops for swimming and snorkeling in calm lagoon waters.

experiences.name: Silves Castle & Old Town Food Walk
experiences.description: Explore the Moorish red sandstone castle of Silves, the ancient Algarve capital, followed by a guided food walk through the historic old town. Sample local specialties including carob products, medronho brandy, almond sweets, and fresh orange juice at traditional market stalls.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Portugal Algarve
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Boutique Taghostel
hotel.location: Rua Dr. Faria e Silva, 32, Lagos, PT (37.1038,-8.6730)

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Faro Airport at 22:30. Take the budget-friendly Eva Bus or Rede Expressos coach from Faro Airport to Lagos (approx. €6-8, ~1.5 hours). Check in to Boutique Taghostel on Rua Dr. Faria e Silva. Freshen up and get settled.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or airport snack
meals.lunch: On the plane or airport snack
meals.dinner: Grab a late-night snack at a 24h petrol station kiosk near the bus terminal or a kebab shop near Lagos center (€3-5)

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book the Faro-Lagos bus ticket online to save time. The hostel is a short walk or cheap taxi (~€5) from Lagos bus station. Keep energy for tomorrow — big beach day ahead!

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. Enjoy the hostel's communal breakfast if included, or head to a local pastelaria for a classic Portuguese breakfast of pastel de nata and galão coffee (€2-3). Stroll through Lagos old town, explore the historic Praça Gil Eanes and the Igreja de Santo António.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take a short local bus to Meia Praia, Lagos's longest and most accessible beach (free entry). Swim, relax, and soak up the September sun. Rent a beach umbrella and chair for ~€5-8 if needed. Explore the golden cliffs along the shoreline.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos town center. Walk along the marina and watch the sunset over the Bensafrim River. Explore the lively Rua 25 de Abril for budget tapas bars and cervejarias.

meals.breakfast: Pastelaria Mulato near Lagos center — pastel de nata + galão (€2-3)
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic from the local Pingo Doce supermarket near the bus station — bread, cheese, ham, fruit (€4-6)
meals.dinner: O Camilo or a local tasca on Rua 25 de Abril — prato do dia (dish of the day) with soup, main, and drink (€8-10)

day_by_day.notes: September is ideal — warm sea temperatures (~22°C), fewer crowds than August, and lower prices. Meia Praia is a 10-minute walk or free bus ride from the hostel.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning visit to Praia Dona Ana, one of the most scenic beaches near Lagos (~20-minute walk from the hostel). Arrive early to claim a good spot among the dramatic ochre rock formations. Swim in the crystal-clear turquoise water.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk the coastal cliff path from Dona Ana toward Praia do Camilo and Ponta da Piedade. The Ponta da Piedade sea caves and grottos are a must-see — take a kayak tour from the beach (€15-20 per person) or admire from the clifftop viewpoint for free. Return to Lagos by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Mercado de Lagos (covered market) area. Join fellow hostel guests for a social evening — many hostels organize free or cheap communal dinners or bar crawls.

meals.breakfast: Hostel breakfast or grab a bifana (pork sandwich) from a local café (€2)
meals.lunch: Snack bar at Praia Dona Ana — grilled sardines or a tosta mista (€5-7)
meals.dinner: Tasca do Celso or similar local restaurant in Lagos old town — grilled fish or cataplana for one (€9-12)

day_by_day.notes: The cliff walk from Dona Ana to Ponta da Piedade is approximately 2km and takes about 45 minutes. Wear sturdy sandals or trainers. The kayak tour is highly recommended and worth the splurge.

day_by_day.morning: Take a local Rede Expressos or Eva Bus to Sagres (~45 min, €3-4 each way). Visit the impressive Fortaleza de Sagres (€3 entry) — a 15th-century fortress at the southwestern tip of Europe with dramatic Atlantic views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to Praia do Martinhal or Praia da Mareta in Sagres — quieter, wilder beaches with powerful Atlantic waves. If you're feeling adventurous, rent a surfboard or take a beginner surf lesson (€25-30 including board and wetsuit). Sagres is one of Europe's top surf destinations.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos by bus. Enjoy a relaxed evening in the hostel common area. Chat with fellow travelers and plan the next few days.

meals.breakfast: Quick café stop in Lagos before the bus — toast with manteiga and coffee (€2)
meals.lunch: A Tasca in Sagres village — fresh tuna steak or grilled limpets (percebes) with local bread (€8-10)
meals.dinner: Supermarket dinner back in Lagos — rotisserie chicken from Pingo Doce + salad + local Algarve wine (€6-8)

day_by_day.notes: Sagres is the windiest point in the Algarve — bring a light jacket even in September. The last bus back to Lagos is usually around 19:00-20:00, so check the schedule in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Lagos Saturday market (Mercado Municipal) for fresh local produce, cheeses, smoked sausages, and Algarve almonds and figs. Stock up on cheap, quality snacks. Then explore the Museu de Lagos (€3 entry) to learn about the city's Moorish and Age of Discovery history.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Praia da Luz, a charming village beach 6km west of Lagos. Take the local bus (€1.50) or rent a bicycle from the hostel (~€10/day). Swim and relax on the wide sandy beach backed by white-washed village houses. Explore the small village.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos for the evening. Walk the old town walls and enjoy the golden hour light on the historic buildings. Find a miradouro (viewpoint) for sunset views.

meals.breakfast: Fresh fruit, local cheese, and bread from the Saturday market (€3-4)
meals.lunch: Snack bar at Praia da Luz — prego no pão (steak sandwich) and a beer (€6-8)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Adega da Marina in Lagos — affordable seafood rice or grilled dourada (sea bream) (€10-12)

day_by_day.notes: Saturday market is busiest in the morning — arrive by 9:00 for the best selection. Praia da Luz is a great alternative to busier Lagos beaches and has a lovely village atmosphere.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Portimão (~30 min by bus, €2.50). Visit the Museu de Portimão (free on Sundays until 14:00) — a fascinating former sardine canning factory turned museum. Explore the riverside promenade.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take a short taxi to Praia da Rocha, one of the Algarve's most famous beaches — a wide golden stretch backed by dramatic red cliffs. Swim and explore the sea caves accessible at low tide. Walk the clifftop promenade for panoramic views.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos by bus. Sunday evening is perfect for a quiet wine tasting session — visit a local wine shop in Lagos and pick up a bottle of Algarve regional wine (Vida Nova or Quinta dos Vales labels, €5-8) to enjoy on the hostel terrace.

meals.breakfast: Café in Portimão near the museum — croissant and coffee (€2-3)
meals.lunch: Portimão is famous for grilled sardines — eat at one of the riverside tascas near the old fish market (€7-9)
meals.dinner: Self-catering at the hostel — local wine, cheese, presunto (cured ham), and olives from the supermarket (€8-10)

day_by_day.notes: Museu de Portimão is free on Sunday mornings — a great budget win. Praia da Rocha can be crowded even in September on weekends, so arrive early for a good spot.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recharge day. Sleep in, enjoy a slow hostel breakfast, and do laundry (most hostels have washing machines for €3-4). Browse the Lagos town center boutiques and souvenir shops along Rua 25 de Abril.
day_by_day.afternoon: Wine tasting experience at a local Lagos wine bar or shop. Look for free or low-cost tastings at Garrafeira Soares or similar wine merchants in town. Focus on Algarve DOC wines — try Negra Mole and Crato Branco grape varieties. Alternatively, visit the nearby Quinta da Penina or book a budget winery tour (~€10-15 including tastings).
day_by_day.evening: Sunset drinks at a rooftop bar or clifftop bar in Lagos. Stevie Ray's Jazz Bar or Bon Vivant are popular and affordable. Enjoy the relaxed Monday evening atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Hostel breakfast or local café — yogurt, fruit, and coffee (€3-4)
meals.lunch: Mercado de Lagos food court — fresh grilled fish or a bifana (€5-7)
meals.dinner: Restaurante O Galeão in Lagos old town — traditional Portuguese cozido or bacalhau dish (€9-11)

day_by_day.notes: This is a good day to plan the second week of the trip, book any remaining activities, and rest tired legs. Many wineries require advance booking — call ahead or book online.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early bus to Albufeira (~1.5 hours, €5-6). Explore the charming old town (Albufeira Velha) before the crowds arrive — whitewashed streets, the fishermen's beach tunnel, and the clifftop Igreja Matriz.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Praia dos Pescadores (Fishermen's Beach) in Albufeira old town — a lively, scenic beach right in the heart of the village. Walk east along the cliff path to Praia da Oura for a quieter alternative. Swim and enjoy the warm September sea.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Albufeira's famous Rua Cândido dos Reis (The Strip) for a lively evening atmosphere. Have a drink at a budget bar before catching the last bus back to Lagos (~20:00-21:00).

meals.breakfast: On the bus or quick café stop in Albufeira (€2-3)
meals.lunch: Snack bar on Praia dos Pescadores — grilled chicken piri-piri wrap and a Sagres beer (€7-9)
meals.dinner: Quick dinner in Albufeira before the bus — a local tasca prato do dia (€8-10) or grab food to go

day_by_day.notes: Albufeira is more touristy than Lagos but worth a day visit. Check the return bus schedule carefully — the last bus to Lagos can be early. Consider a taxi share with hostel friends if you miss it (~€25-30 split).

day_by_day.morning: Rent a bicycle from the hostel or a local shop (~€10-12/day) and cycle the Via Algarviana coastal path or the quiet back roads toward Burgau village (~8km west of Lagos). Enjoy the rural Algarve countryside — fig trees, carob trees, and wildflowers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Praia de Burgau — a small, sheltered, and relatively uncrowded beach in a picturesque fishing village. Swim, snorkel (bring your own mask or rent for €3), and explore the village. Cycle back to Lagos along the coastal road in the late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Treat yourself to a proper sit-down dinner in Lagos to celebrate the halfway point of the trip. Find a restaurant with a good-value tourist menu (menu turístico) — typically €12-15 for three courses with wine.

meals.breakfast: Hostel or local café before cycling — toast, eggs, and coffee (€3-4)
meals.lunch: Bar/restaurant in Burgau village — fresh grilled fish of the day with salad and chips (€9-11)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Casinha do Petisco in Lagos — three-course menu turístico with local wine (€12-15)

day_by_day.notes: The cycle to Burgau is mostly flat with some gentle hills — suitable for all fitness levels. Bring sunscreen, water, and a small backpack. September light is beautiful for cycling — not too hot.

day_by_day.morning: Take a bus to Silves (~1 hour, €3-4) — the ancient Moorish capital of the Algarve. Visit the magnificent red sandstone Castelo de Silves (€2.80 entry) with panoramic views over orange groves and the Arade River valley.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Silves old town — the Gothic Sé Catedral (free entry), the Museu Arqueológico (€2), and the charming riverside promenade. Silves is surrounded by vineyards and citrus orchards — this is prime wine country. Visit a local adega (wine cellar) for an informal tasting of Algarve wines (often free or €5-8).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos by bus. Enjoy a quiet evening at the hostel — share travel stories with fellow guests and plan the final days of the trip.

meals.breakfast: Café in Silves near the castle — pastel de nata and coffee (€2)
meals.lunch: Restaurante Marisqueira Rui in Silves — famous for cataplana and fresh river fish (€10-13)
meals.dinner: Self-catering at the hostel — local Silves wine purchased from the adega + supermarket snacks (€6-8)

day_by_day.notes: Silves is one of the most historically rich towns in the Algarve and often overlooked by tourists. The castle is especially beautiful in the late afternoon golden light. Silves also hosts a Medieval Fair in August — September is quieter and cheaper.

day_by_day.morning: Full beach day at Praia do Camilo — arguably the most beautiful beach near Lagos, accessible via a wooden staircase down dramatic cliffs. Arrive early (before 10:00) to secure a spot in this small but stunning cove. Swim in the incredibly clear water.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk the cliff path from Camilo to Ponta da Piedade lighthouse and viewpoint (free). The late afternoon light on the golden rock formations is spectacular. Take photos and enjoy the peaceful atmosphere as day-trippers leave. Walk back to Lagos along the coastal path (~45 minutes).
day_by_day.evening: Final big night out in Lagos. Join a hostel pub crawl or explore the bars on Rua 25 de Abril and Rua Soeiro da Costa. Try a ginjinha (cherry liqueur) shot at a local bar (€1-2). Dance at one of the late-night bars.

meals.breakfast: Hostel breakfast or café — full Portuguese breakfast with eggs, toast, and coffee (€4-5)
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic from the supermarket to eat on Praia do Camilo — sandwiches, fruit, and local pastries (€5-6)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Nah Nah Bah in Lagos — burgers and craft beer, popular with backpackers (€10-12)

day_by_day.notes: Praia do Camilo has very limited space — arrive early or visit on a weekday morning. The cliff path to Ponta da Piedade is one of the most scenic walks in the entire Algarve. Wear good shoes.

day_by_day.morning: Take a morning bus to Tavira (~2.5 hours, €8-10) — one of the most beautiful and authentic towns in the Algarve. Explore the Roman bridge, the castle ruins, and the charming whitewashed old town with its distinctive four-sided rooftops.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the ferry from Tavira to Ilha de Tavira (€1.50 return) — a stunning barrier island beach with crystal-clear lagoon water and fine white sand. This is one of the best beaches in the entire Algarve and relatively uncrowded in September. Swim, relax, and enjoy the natural beauty of the Ria Formosa Natural Park.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos by bus (check schedule — last bus may be around 18:00-19:00). Enjoy a final relaxed evening in Lagos — sunset walk along the marina and a farewell dinner.

meals.breakfast: Quick café in Lagos before the bus (€2-3)
meals.lunch: Beach snack bar on Ilha de Tavira — fresh seafood, grilled fish, or a simple salad (€8-10)
meals.dinner: O Camilo restaurant in Lagos or a local tasca — celebratory final dinner with grilled sea bass and local wine (€12-15)

day_by_day.notes: Tavira is a long day trip from Lagos — start early. The Ilha de Tavira ferry runs frequently in summer/early autumn. Tavira is considered one of Portugal's most beautiful towns and is well worth the journey.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Lagos. Wake up early for one last sunrise walk to Ponta da Piedade or Praia Dona Ana. Take final photos and soak in the Algarve atmosphere. Return to the hostel for checkout.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of Boutique Taghostel (standard checkout 11:00 — ask to store luggage if needed). Spend the final afternoon exploring any missed spots in Lagos old town. Visit the Slave Market Museum (Mercado de Escravos, €3) — the only surviving slave market building in Europe. Browse souvenir shops for last-minute gifts — local honey, almond sweets (Dom Rodrigos), and Algarve wine make great budget souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Take the Eva Bus or Rede Expressos from Lagos to Faro Airport for your departure flight. Allow at least 2.5 hours travel time plus airport check-in. Reflect on an incredible 13 days in the Algarve!

meals.breakfast: Final pastel de nata and galão at a Lagos café — a proper Portuguese farewell (€2-3)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the Lagos market or a café near the bus station — soup and sandwich (€5-6)
meals.dinner: Airport café or snack at Faro Airport before departure (€8-12)

day_by_day.notes: Lagos to Faro Airport by bus takes approximately 1.5-2 hours with a possible change in Portimão or Albufeira. Check the Sunday bus schedule in advance as services may be less frequent. Budget tip: buy a small bottle of local Algarve wine at the supermarket as a final souvenir — it's much cheaper than at the airport!

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Faro Airport at 22:30. Take the airport shuttle or pre-booked taxi (~1 hour) to Boutique Taghostel in Lagos. Check in, freshen up, and grab a late-night snack at a nearby 24-hour café or the hostel's common area. Get oriented with a map of Lagos for the days ahead.

meals.breakfast: On the plane
meals.lunch: On the plane or at the airport
meals.dinner: Late-night snack at Café Ginginha or a nearby petiscos bar still open near Rua Dr. Faria e Silva – try a pastel de nata and a glass of local wine to welcome yourself to Portugal

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light – only arrival activities. Pre-book your taxi from Faro Airport in advance to avoid long queues late at night. Confirm hostel late check-in arrangements before travel.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Lagos Old Town on foot. Stroll through the historic center, visit the Igreja de Santo António (a stunning baroque church), and walk along the old city walls. Stop at the Slave Market Museum (Mercado de Escravos) for a dose of history. End the walk at Ponta da Bandeira Fort overlooking the marina.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Meia Praia, Lagos's longest beach (a short taxi or bus ride east of town). Spend the afternoon swimming in calm Atlantic waters, sunbathing on golden sands, and renting a paddleboard or kayak from a beach vendor. The beach is less crowded in September – perfect for a relaxed first full beach day.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos town center. Wander Rua 25 de Abril for tapas bars and local wine. Enjoy a leisurely dinner at a mid-range restaurant in the old town.

meals.breakfast: Café Correia near the hostel – fresh bread, local cheese, ham, and a galão (milky espresso) for a classic Portuguese breakfast (~€5–7)
meals.lunch: Beach snack bar at Meia Praia – grilled sardines, salad, and a cold Sagres beer (~€12–15)
meals.dinner: O Camilo Restaurant or Adega da Marina – try grilled sea bass (robalo) with roasted potatoes and a glass of Algarve white wine (~€20–25 per person)

day_by_day.notes: September weather in the Algarve is typically warm (24–28°C) with minimal rain – ideal beach conditions. Bring sunscreen, a hat, and reusable water bottle. Lagos old town is very walkable from the hostel.

day_by_day.morning: Join the Praia da Marinha Coastal Hike & Swim experience. Depart from Lagos by local bus or organized tour pickup. Hike the dramatic clifftop trail between Praia da Marinha and Praia de Benagil, marveling at golden limestone arches, hidden grottos, and turquoise coves. The trail is approximately 5 km and takes 2–3 hours with stops.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend to Praia da Marinha beach for a swim in the crystal-clear water surrounded by towering cliffs. Explore the small sea caves accessible from the beach at low tide. Relax on the beach and soak in one of the Algarve's most photogenic settings.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos by bus or taxi. Shower and change at the hostel, then head out for a relaxed evening in the Praça Gil Eanes square area.

meals.breakfast: At the hostel or a nearby padaria (bakery) – toast with butter and jam, fresh orange juice, and espresso (~€4–6)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or snacks from a local deli before departure – local cheese, chouriço, bread, and fruit (~€6–8). There are limited food options near Praia da Marinha.
meals.dinner: Restaurante Adega da Marina in Lagos – cataplana de marisco (seafood stew) for two, paired with a local Lagoa wine (~€22–28 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Wear sturdy walking shoes for the coastal hike – the clifftop paths can be uneven. Bring plenty of water (at least 1.5L per person). Check tide times before descending to beach caves. Book the experience in advance as September is still busy.

day_by_day.morning: Take a morning bus or taxi to Sagres (about 30 minutes west of Lagos). Visit the dramatic Fortaleza de Sagres, a 15th-century fortress perched on a windswept promontory at the southwestern tip of Europe. Explore the wind compass (Rosa dos Ventos) and enjoy breathtaking Atlantic views. Walk along the clifftops to Cabo de São Vicente – the most southwestern point of continental Europe.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Praia do Beliche or Praia da Mareta in Sagres for an afternoon swim. These beaches are sheltered and beautiful, with calmer waters than the exposed Atlantic-facing beaches. Rent a surfboard or bodyboard if feeling adventurous – Sagres is a surf hub.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos. Enjoy a relaxed evening exploring the marina area and the lively bar scene on Rua Candido dos Reis.

meals.breakfast: Café near the hostel – croissant, fresh fruit, and coffee (~€5)
meals.lunch: A Sagres – local restaurant near the fortress serving fresh fish of the day with salad and bread (~€14–18 per person)
meals.dinner: : Restaurante Bon Vivant in Lagos – Mediterranean-inspired menu with local ingredients; try the tuna steak with sweet potato (~€20–25 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Sagres can be windy even on warm days – bring a light jacket. The bus from Lagos to Sagres runs regularly and costs around €4 each way. Cabo de São Vicente is a must-see sunset spot if you time your visit right.

day_by_day.morning: Join the Benagil Sea Cave Kayak Tour. Depart from Carvoeiro or Benagil beach (approximately 45 minutes east of Lagos by car or taxi). Paddle through the iconic Benagil Cave – a cathedral-like sea cave with a natural skylight – and explore surrounding sea arches and hidden beaches accessible only by water. Tours typically last 2–3 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the kayak tour, relax at Praia de Benagil or nearby Praia de Carvalho. These small, sheltered cove beaches are among the most beautiful in the Algarve. Swim, snorkel, or simply rest on the sand.
day_by_day.evening: Head into Carvoeiro village for the evening – a charming fishing village with whitewashed houses, clifftop views, and excellent seafood restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hostel or a café in Lagos before departure – toast, eggs, and coffee (~€6–8)
meals.lunch: Snack bar at Praia de Benagil or Carvoeiro – fresh grilled fish sandwich and a cold drink (~€10–13)
meals.dinner: Restaurante O Castelo in Carvoeiro – grilled octopus salad starter, followed by arroz de lingueirão (razor clam rice); local Lagoa wine (~€22–27 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book the Benagil Kayak Tour well in advance – it is one of the most popular experiences in the Algarve and fills up quickly, especially on weekends. Wear a swimsuit under your clothes and bring a dry bag for valuables. Arrange a taxi or rideshare from Lagos to Benagil (~€25–30 each way).

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recharge morning. Sleep in, enjoy a leisurely breakfast, and spend time at the hostel's common area meeting fellow travelers. Take a slow walk to Praia de Dona Ana – one of Lagos's most iconic beaches, just a 15-minute walk from the hostel. Admire the dramatic ochre cliffs and swim in the calm cove.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Lagos Municipal Market (Mercado Municipal) if open, or browse the artisan shops and boutiques along Rua 25 de Abril. Pick up local ceramics, cork products, or Algarve honey as souvenirs. Visit the Lagos Zoo if interested (about 10 minutes by taxi).
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner drinks at a clifftop bar near Ponta da Piedade – watch the golden hour light illuminate the famous rock formations. Then dinner in the old town.

meals.breakfast: Hostel breakfast or Pastelaria Mota – full Portuguese breakfast with eggs, presunto (cured ham), cheese, and fresh juice (~€7–9)
meals.lunch: Picnic on Praia de Dona Ana – grab supplies from a local supermarket (Pingo Doce nearby): local cheese, olives, bread, fruit, and a bottle of Algarve rosé (~€10–12 total)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Casinha do Petisco – traditional Portuguese petiscos (small plates) style dining; try the bacalhau à brás (shredded salt cod with eggs and potatoes) (~€18–22 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Sunday is a good day to slow down and explore Lagos itself rather than traveling far. Ponta da Piedade at sunset is spectacular – arrive 30–40 minutes before sunset for the best light and to secure a good viewing spot.

day_by_day.morning: Join the Algarve Wine & Cataplana Tasting Experience. Travel to the Lagoa wine region (approximately 40 minutes east of Lagos). Visit a local winery for a guided tour of the vineyards and cellar, learning about the unique Algarve terroir and indigenous grape varieties like Negra Mole and Crato Branco. Enjoy a structured tasting of 4–5 wines.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the experience with a traditional cataplana cooking demonstration and tasting lunch at the winery. The cataplana – a copper clam-shaped pot – is the iconic cooking vessel of the Algarve, used to slow-cook seafood and meat stews. Pair the meal with the wines tasted earlier.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos in the late afternoon. Spend a quiet evening strolling the marina, watching the boats, and enjoying a nightcap at a wine bar.

meals.breakfast: Café near the hostel – pastéis de nata, coffee, and fresh orange juice (~€5–6)
meals.lunch: Included in the Algarve Wine & Cataplana Tasting Experience – a full cataplana meal with wine pairings
meals.dinner: Light dinner at Taberna de Lagos – charcuterie board with local Algarve wines, olives, and regional cheeses (~€15–18 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book the wine and cataplana experience in advance. Many wineries in the Lagoa region offer transport from Lagos – confirm pickup arrangements when booking. Designate a non-drinking member of the group if driving, or arrange a taxi. This is a highlight experience for wine lovers.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Silves – join the Silves Castle & Old Town Food Walk experience. Travel by train from Lagos to Silves (approximately 40 minutes, scenic route through the Algarve countryside). Explore the magnificent red sandstone Moorish castle (Castelo de Silves), one of the best-preserved in Portugal, with panoramic views over orange groves and the Arade River valley.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the guided food walk through Silves old town. Sample local specialties including medronho (arbutus berry spirit), almond sweets, smoked sausages, and traditional Algarve pastries at artisan shops and local producers. Visit the Silves Cathedral (Sé de Silves) and the Archaeological Museum.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos by train. Enjoy a relaxed evening with dinner near the hostel.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast at Lagos train station café before departure – toast and coffee (~€4–5)
meals.lunch: Included in the Silves food walk experience – tastings throughout the old town
meals.dinner: Restaurante Nah Nah Bah in Lagos – gourmet burgers with local Algarve beef and craft beer; a more casual mid-week dinner (~€14–18 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Lagos–Silves train runs several times daily and costs approximately €3–4 each way. Silves is a quieter, more authentic Algarve town – a wonderful contrast to the coastal beach scene. The castle entrance fee is around €3. Wear comfortable shoes for the cobblestone streets.

day_by_day.morning: Beach day at Praia da Luz, a charming village beach about 6 km west of Lagos (reachable by local bus in 15 minutes). The beach is wide, sandy, and backed by a dramatic black volcanic rock formation. Swim, snorkel around the rocks, or simply relax. The village of Luz has a lovely promenade for a morning stroll.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a bicycle in Lagos and cycle the coastal path westward toward Burgau and Salema – two authentic fishing villages with beautiful beaches. The route passes through rolling hills and offers stunning sea views. Stop for a swim at Praia de Salema, a picturesque village beach.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos by bus or taxi (leave the bike in Lagos before cycling out, or arrange a return). Dinner in the old town.

meals.breakfast: Padaria Portuguesa near the hostel – fresh bread rolls, butter, local honey, and coffee (~€5–7)
meals.lunch: Snack bar at Praia da Luz or Burgau – grilled chicken piri-piri wrap and a cold drink (~€10–13)
meals.dinner: Restaurante A Forja in Lagos – traditional Algarvian cuisine; try the frango no churrasco (charcoal chicken) with piri-piri sauce and fries (~€16–20 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Bicycle rentals are available in Lagos for approximately €15–20 per day. The coastal cycling route to Salema is moderately hilly – suitable for average fitness levels. Bring plenty of water and sunscreen. September evenings are warm enough to dine outdoors.

day_by_day.morning: Take a dolphin watching boat tour from Lagos Marina. The Algarve coast is home to bottlenose and common dolphins, and September is an excellent month for sightings. Tours typically last 2–3 hours and often include snorkeling stops at sea caves and grottos along the coastline.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the boat tour, visit Praia do Camilo – a small, dramatic cove beach reached by a wooden staircase carved into the cliffs, just south of Lagos. One of the most beautiful and intimate beaches in the area. Swim and relax in the sheltered cove.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset walk along the clifftops from Praia do Camilo to Ponta da Piedade. Watch the sun dip into the Atlantic from the lighthouse viewpoint. Return to Lagos for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Café Ginginha near the hostel – full breakfast with eggs, toast, and fresh juice (~€7–9)
meals.lunch: Snack bar near Lagos Marina post-tour – fresh fish tacos and a cold beer (~€12–15)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Dom Sebastião in Lagos – upscale mid-range dining; try the cataplana de peixe (fish cataplana) with a bottle of Algarve white wine (~€25–30 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book the dolphin watching tour in advance through the Lagos Marina operators. Tours cost approximately €35–45 per person. Bring a light jacket for the boat – it can be breezy on the water even in September. The Ponta da Piedade sunset walk is one of the most memorable experiences of the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Portimão and Praia da Rocha. Take the local bus or train to Portimão (20 minutes from Lagos). Visit the Museu de Portimão – an excellent free museum housed in a former sardine canning factory, telling the story of the Algarve's fishing heritage. Walk along the Portimão riverfront promenade.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Praia da Rocha – one of the Algarve's most famous beaches, with a wide golden sand bay backed by dramatic red cliffs. Spend the afternoon swimming and relaxing. Explore the clifftop promenade with its bars and viewpoints. Visit the small Fortaleza de Santa Catarina at the eastern end of the beach.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Portimão for dinner before returning to Lagos. Portimão is famous for its grilled sardines – a must-try.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast at the hostel before departure – yogurt, fruit, and coffee (~€5)
meals.lunch: Tasca do Celso in Portimão – famous for grilled sardines served on bread with salad; a true local institution (~€12–16 per person)
meals.dinner: Taberna da Maré in Portimão – fresh seafood platters with local wine before the bus back to Lagos (~€20–24 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Museu de Portimão is free on Sunday afternoons but charges a small fee (~€3) on other days. Portimão is easily reached by bus from Lagos (Eva Bus, approximately €3 each way). Praia da Rocha can be crowded on weekends – arrive early for a good spot.

day_by_day.morning: Morning yoga or wellness session – many Lagos hostels and studios offer morning yoga classes, often with ocean views. Check with Boutique Taghostel for recommendations. Alternatively, take a peaceful early morning walk along the Lagos coastline before the crowds arrive, visiting Praia de Porto de Mós – a wide, less-visited beach south of Lagos.
day_by_day.afternoon: Algarve wine afternoon – visit a local wine shop in Lagos (such as Garrafeira do Mercado) for a self-guided tasting of Algarve wines. Purchase a selection of bottles to enjoy over the remaining days. Then spend the afternoon at Praia de Porto de Mós, swimming and relaxing on the quieter end of the beach.
day_by_day.evening: Final big night out in Lagos. Explore the vibrant nightlife scene – start with cocktails at a rooftop bar, then dinner at a top restaurant, followed by drinks on Rua Candido dos Reis (the main bar street).

meals.breakfast: Hostel breakfast or local café – avocado toast with poached eggs and coffee; a slightly indulgent start to the penultimate day (~€8–10)
meals.lunch: Snack bar at Praia de Porto de Mós – grilled chicken, salad, and a cold Algarve rosé (~€13–16)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Vasco da Gama in Lagos – splurge slightly for the last big dinner; try the lobster rice (arroz de lagosta) or the mixed seafood grill (~€28–35 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Saturday night in Lagos is lively – the town has a great mix of locals and international visitors. The bar scene on Rua Candido dos Reis gets going after 22:00. If you prefer a quieter evening, the marina area has lovely waterfront bars with live music.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in the Algarve. Wake up early for one last sunrise walk to Ponta da Piedade – the golden morning light on the limestone rock formations is magical and different from the sunset experience. Take photos, breathe in the Atlantic air, and say goodbye to the Algarve coast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the hostel, check out, and store luggage. Spend the remaining time in Lagos doing any last-minute shopping – pick up local products like Algarve olive oil, almond sweets (Dom Rodrigo), medronho spirit, or local wine. Take a final stroll through the old town.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Lagos for Faro Airport (allow 1–1.5 hours travel time by taxi or shuttle). Reflect on 13 wonderful days of beaches, wine, food, and culture in the Algarve.

meals.breakfast: Final Portuguese breakfast at Café Correia – pastel de nata, galão, and fresh orange juice; a perfect farewell to Portugal (~€5–7)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a café near the hostel before checkout – soup, bread, and a glass of local wine (~€10–12)
meals.dinner: Airport or in-flight meal – or grab a final bifana (pork sandwich) at a café near Faro Airport (~€4–6)

day_by_day.notes: Check your flight departure time carefully and allow sufficient time to reach Faro Airport. A taxi from Lagos to Faro Airport costs approximately €50–65 and takes about 60–75 minutes. Pre-book the taxi the night before. Confirm hostel checkout time and arrange luggage storage if needed for the final afternoon.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Portugal Algarve Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Boutique Taghostel
hotel.location: Rua Dr. Faria e Silva, 32, Lagos, PT (37.1038,-8.6730)

experiences.name: Praia da Marinha Coastal Hike & Swim
experiences.description: Explore one of the Algarve's most stunning beaches, known for its dramatic limestone cliffs, sea caves, and crystal-clear turquoise waters. Hike the clifftop trail from Benagil and descend to the secluded cove for a refreshing swim.

experiences.name: Benagil Sea Cave Kayak Tour
experiences.description: Paddle through the iconic Benagil Cave, one of the world's most beautiful sea caves, accessible only by water. A guided kayak tour takes you through hidden grottos and arches along the golden coastline, offering a unique perspective of the Algarve's dramatic geology.

experiences.name: Algarve Wine & Cataplana Tasting Experience
experiences.description: Visit a local winery in the Lagoa wine region, the heart of Algarve viticulture, for a guided tasting of regional wines including Arinto and Negra Mole varieties. Pair your wines with a traditional Cataplana seafood stew prepared by a local chef.

experiences.name: Ria Formosa Natural Park Boat Tour
experiences.description: Cruise through the stunning Ria Formosa lagoon system, a protected natural park spanning 60km of coastline. Discover barrier islands, flamingo colonies, and secluded barrier beaches only accessible by boat, with stops for swimming and snorkeling in calm lagoon waters.

experiences.name: Silves Castle & Old Town Food Walk
experiences.description: Explore the Moorish red sandstone castle of Silves, the ancient Algarve capital, followed by a guided food walk through the historic old town. Sample local specialties including carob products, medronho brandy, almond sweets, and fresh orange juice at traditional market stalls.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Arrival day
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - Arrival day
day_by_day.evening: Late arrival at Faro Airport at 22:30. Private luxury transfer arranged from Faro Airport to Boutique Taghostel in Lagos (~1 hour). Check in, unwind with a welcome glass of local Algarve wine provided by the hotel, and settle into your boutique suite.

meals.breakfast: N/A - In-flight
meals.lunch: N/A - In-flight
meals.dinner: Light late-night charcuterie and cheese board with local wines arranged by the hotel upon arrival, or a quick bite at the hotel's lounge bar.

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange private airport transfer in advance. Confirm late check-in with Boutique Taghostel. Keep Day 1 light — rest is the priority after a long-haul flight.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely late breakfast at the hotel, then take a gentle orientation stroll through Lagos Old Town. Explore the historic Ponta da Bandeira Fort, the charming cobblestone streets, and the vibrant local market. Stop at a local pastelaria for a mid-morning espresso and pastel de nata.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Meia Praia Beach, one of the longest and most pristine beaches near Lagos. Arrange a premium beach club experience with sun loungers, parasols, and waiter service. Enjoy the warm September Atlantic waters and dramatic coastal scenery.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at a clifftop bar overlooking the Lagos coastline. Dinner at a top Lagos restaurant such as Vistas Restaurant or Casinha do Petisco, featuring modern Portuguese cuisine with fresh Algarve seafood.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet breakfast at Boutique Taghostel — fresh pastries, local cheeses, cured meats, fruit, and specialty coffee.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the Meia Praia beach club — grilled fish, fresh salads, and chilled Vinho Verde.
meals.dinner: Fine dining at a top Lagos restaurant — recommend grilled sea bass, cataplana de marisco, and a bottle of Algarve regional white wine.

day_by_day.notes: September weather in the Algarve is typically warm and sunny (24–28°C), perfect for beach days. Bring reef-safe sunscreen and stay hydrated.

day_by_day.morning: Praia da Marinha Coastal Hike & Swim — depart early from Lagos (~30-minute drive east). Explore one of the Algarve's most stunning beaches, known for its dramatic limestone cliffs, golden sea arches, and crystal-clear turquoise waters. A guided coastal hike reveals hidden grottos and panoramic cliff-top views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the Praia da Marinha area — swim in the sheltered coves, snorkel among the rock formations, and relax on the golden sands. Alternatively, visit nearby Praia de Benagil for a preview of tomorrow's kayak adventure.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos. Freshen up and enjoy a premium dinner at Restaurante Adega da Marina or a comparable fine dining venue in Lagos, specializing in fresh Atlantic seafood and regional Algarve dishes.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at the hotel before departure.
meals.lunch: Packed premium picnic lunch arranged by the hotel, or dine at a clifftop restaurant near Praia da Marinha — grilled octopus, local bread, and chilled rosé.
meals.dinner: Upscale dinner in Lagos — try the arroz de lingueirão (razor clam rice) or grilled turbot with local wines.

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable hiking shoes with grip for the coastal trail. The hike involves some uneven terrain and steps down to the beach. Bring water, sunscreen, and a light layer for the breeze.

day_by_day.morning: Benagil Sea Cave Kayak Tour — depart from Benagil Beach (~35 minutes from Lagos). Paddle through the world-famous Benagil Cave, a breathtaking sea cathedral with a natural skylight dome. A professional guide leads the small-group or private tour through sea caves, arches, and hidden beaches inaccessible by land.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the kayak tour, relax on Praia de Benagil or nearby Praia do Carvalho. Enjoy a leisurely afternoon swim and sunbathe on the secluded golden sands surrounded by towering limestone cliffs.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos. Sunset drinks on the hotel terrace or at a rooftop bar. Dinner at a premium Lagos restaurant — consider O Camilo, perched dramatically on the cliffs above Praia do Camilo, offering spectacular ocean views and exceptional seafood.

meals.breakfast: Early gourmet breakfast at the hotel before the kayak tour.
meals.lunch: Seafood lunch at a restaurant near Benagil or Carvoeiro — fresh grilled fish, local salads, and chilled white wine.
meals.dinner: Cliff-top fine dining at O Camilo or equivalent — grilled lobster, fresh percebes (barnacles), and a premium Algarve wine selection.

day_by_day.notes: Book the Benagil Kayak Tour in advance as spots fill quickly, especially in September. Opt for a private tour for the most exclusive experience. Wear a swimsuit under clothes and bring a dry bag for valuables.

day_by_day.morning: Algarve Wine & Cataplana Tasting Experience — drive to the Lagoa wine region (~40 minutes from Lagos), the heart of Algarve viticulture. Enjoy a guided winery tour through the vineyards, learning about the unique terroir and indigenous grape varieties such as Negra Mole and Crato Branco.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the wine experience with a premium tasting of multiple Algarve wines paired with a traditional Cataplana feast — a slow-cooked copper pot dish of clams, prawns, chorizo, and vegetables. Explore the winery cellars and meet the winemaker for an exclusive behind-the-scenes experience.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos in the late afternoon. Relax at the hotel with a spa treatment or a quiet evening stroll through the old town. Light dinner at a wine bar in Lagos, continuing the wine theme with a curated Portuguese cheese and charcuterie board.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at the hotel.
meals.lunch: Included as part of the Cataplana tasting experience at the winery — a full traditional feast with wine pairings.
meals.dinner: Light evening at a Lagos wine bar — premium Portuguese cheeses, presunto (cured ham), local olives, and a glass of aged Algarve red wine.

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private transport for the winery visit so all guests can enjoy the wine tasting without driving concerns. The Lagoa region is home to several excellent quintas — Quinta dos Vales and Adega do Cantor are highly recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Silves Castle & Old Town Food Walk — drive to Silves (~45 minutes from Lagos), the ancient Moorish capital of the Algarve. Explore the magnificent red sandstone castle, one of the best-preserved Moorish fortifications in Portugal, with panoramic views over the orange groves and Arade River valley.
day_by_day.afternoon: Join a guided food walk through Silves' charming old town, sampling local specialties including almond sweets, fig preserves, smoked sausages, local honey, and traditional Algarvian pastries. Visit the local market and artisan shops. Explore the Gothic Cathedral of Silves.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos. Enjoy a premium dinner at a Lagos fine dining restaurant — consider Restaurante Laranjeira or a comparable venue offering creative modern Portuguese cuisine with Algarve ingredients.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at the hotel.
meals.lunch: Included tastings during the Silves food walk, supplemented by a sit-down lunch at a traditional Silves restaurant — try the local orange-based dishes and grilled meats.
meals.dinner: Elegant dinner in Lagos — slow-roasted suckling pig, black pork from the Alentejo, or fresh Atlantic fish with premium wine pairing.

day_by_day.notes: Silves is particularly beautiful in September when the surrounding orange and almond groves are lush. Wear comfortable walking shoes for the cobblestone streets and castle grounds.

day_by_day.morning: Private yacht charter day — depart from Lagos Marina on a luxury private sailing yacht. Cruise along the stunning Ponta da Piedade coastline, exploring the iconic golden sea stacks, arches, and grottos by boat. Swim and snorkel in the crystal-clear waters of hidden sea caves.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the yacht journey westward toward Sagres and Cabo de São Vicente — the southwesternmost point of continental Europe. Enjoy a gourmet lunch on deck with chilled champagne, fresh seafood, and premium canapés prepared by the yacht's crew. Anchor in a secluded cove for an afternoon swim.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos Marina at sunset for a spectacular golden hour on the water. Freshen up at the hotel and enjoy a celebratory dinner at a premium Lagos restaurant, toasting the halfway point of the trip.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at the hotel before departure.
meals.lunch: Gourmet on-board lunch prepared by the yacht crew — fresh seafood platter, chilled champagne, artisan bread, and premium Portuguese wines.
meals.dinner: Celebratory fine dining dinner in Lagos — tasting menu with wine pairing at the best available restaurant.

day_by_day.notes: Book the private yacht charter well in advance. September offers ideal sailing conditions with warm temperatures and calmer seas. Bring sunscreen, a hat, and a light layer for the sea breeze. Most charters include snorkeling equipment.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Sagres and Cabo de São Vicente. Explore the dramatic windswept cliffs of Europe's southwestern tip — a place of profound historical significance as the launching point of Portugal's Age of Discovery. Visit the Sagres Fortress and the iconic lighthouse at Cabo de São Vicente.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Sagres town and its beautiful beaches — Praia do Martinhal and Praia da Mareta are among the finest in the western Algarve. Enjoy a relaxed afternoon swim and sunbathe on the quieter, more rugged Atlantic beaches of this unspoiled region.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos for a sunset aperitivo on the hotel terrace. Dinner at a premium Lagos restaurant — focus on fresh Atlantic fish and shellfish from the nearby Costa Vicentina.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at the hotel.
meals.lunch: Lunch at a premium Sagres restaurant — try Restaurante Bossa Nova or a comparable venue with fresh local fish and ocean views.
meals.dinner: Elegant dinner in Lagos — grilled whole sea bream, amêijoas à Bulhão Pato (clams in garlic and white wine), and a crisp Algarve white wine.

day_by_day.notes: Sagres and Cabo de São Vicente can be windy even in September — bring a light jacket. The area is a birdwatcher's paradise during autumn migration season. Sunset at Cabo de São Vicente is one of the most spectacular in Europe.

day_by_day.morning: Ria Formosa Natural Park Boat Tour — drive east to Faro (~1.5 hours from Lagos). Board a premium private boat tour through the stunning Ria Formosa lagoon system, a protected natural park spanning 60km of coastline. Cruise through tidal channels, salt marshes, and barrier islands teeming with flamingos, herons, and migratory birds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Disembark on one of the pristine barrier island beaches — Ilha Deserta or Ilha de Tavira — for an afternoon of swimming and relaxation on some of the most unspoiled beaches in Portugal. Enjoy the calm, shallow lagoon waters on one side and the open Atlantic on the other.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back toward Lagos or stay overnight in Faro/Tavira for a change of scenery. Dinner at a premium Faro or Tavira restaurant — the eastern Algarve is renowned for its exceptional seafood and traditional cataplana dishes.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at the hotel before the early departure.
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood lunch on the barrier island or at a lagoon-side restaurant — grilled fish, oysters from the Ria Formosa, and chilled white wine.
meals.dinner: Premium dinner in Faro or Tavira — try Restaurante 2 Passos in Tavira or a comparable fine dining venue specializing in eastern Algarve cuisine.

day_by_day.notes: The Ria Formosa is a UNESCO-listed biosphere reserve. September is an excellent time for birdwatching as migratory species begin to arrive. Book a private boat tour for the most exclusive experience. The drive from Lagos is approximately 1.5 hours — consider hiring a private driver.

day_by_day.morning: Relaxed morning at leisure in Lagos. Sleep in, enjoy a long gourmet breakfast, and spend time exploring the boutique shops and galleries of Lagos Old Town. Visit the Igreja de Santo António, a stunning baroque church with gilded woodwork, and the adjacent Municipal Museum.
day_by_day.afternoon: Praia do Camilo experience — one of the most beautiful and intimate beaches near Lagos, accessed via a wooden staircase through the cliffs. Spend the afternoon swimming in the turquoise waters, exploring the natural rock arches, and relaxing on the golden sands.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at a clifftop bar above Praia do Camilo. Premium dinner at O Camilo restaurant (if not visited earlier) or another top Lagos venue, enjoying the dramatic cliff-top setting and exceptional seafood menu.

meals.breakfast: Extended gourmet breakfast at the hotel — a leisurely morning treat.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a Lagos café or restaurant — fresh salads, grilled fish, and local wine.
meals.dinner: Fine dining at O Camilo or equivalent — fresh lobster, grilled turbot, or the chef's tasting menu with premium wine pairing.

day_by_day.notes: Praia do Camilo is accessed via a steep wooden staircase — wear appropriate footwear. The beach can get busy in the afternoon; arrive early for the best spots. This is a perfect day for recharging before the final days of the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Private jeep safari through the Algarve hinterland — explore the rugged Serra de Monchique mountain range, the highest point in the Algarve. Visit the charming spa town of Caldas de Monchique, known for its thermal springs, and the hilltop village of Monchique with its artisan shops and medronho (arbutus berry brandy) distilleries.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the jeep safari through cork oak forests, citrus groves, and traditional Algarvian farmland. Stop at a local quinta for a tasting of medronho brandy and local honey. Enjoy panoramic views over the entire Algarve coastline from the Fóia summit (902m).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos in the late afternoon. Relaxing evening at the hotel — perhaps a massage or spa treatment. Dinner at a premium Lagos restaurant focusing on inland Algarve cuisine — black pork, wild boar, and mountain herbs.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at the hotel.
meals.lunch: Traditional lunch at a Monchique restaurant — try the local smoked sausages, roast chicken piri-piri, and regional wines.
meals.dinner: Premium dinner in Lagos — Alentejo-style black pork presa, roasted vegetables, and a bold Alentejo red wine.

day_by_day.notes: The Serra de Monchique offers a completely different landscape from the coastal Algarve — lush, green, and cooler. Bring a light layer as temperatures at altitude can be 5–8°C cooler than the coast. The medronho brandy is a unique local specialty worth trying.

day_by_day.morning: Final full beach day — choose your favorite beach from the trip or discover a new one. Praia da Luz (15 minutes from Lagos) offers a beautiful, relaxed bay with golden sand and clear waters, perfect for a final morning swim. Alternatively, revisit Praia da Marinha for a last look at those spectacular cliffs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Lagos for a final afternoon of leisure — browse the artisan shops for premium Portuguese souvenirs (handmade ceramics, cork products, local wines, and olive oils). Visit a local spa for a final indulgent treatment — perhaps a traditional Portuguese massage or a sea salt scrub.
day_by_day.evening: Grand farewell dinner at the finest restaurant in Lagos — a premium tasting menu celebrating the best of Algarve cuisine. Toast the trip with a bottle of premium Algarve wine or a vintage Port. Stroll through the illuminated old town for a final evening in Lagos.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at the hotel — savor every bite of this final morning meal.
meals.lunch: Light beach lunch — fresh grilled fish, salad, and chilled rosé at a beach restaurant.
meals.dinner: Grand farewell tasting menu dinner — the best of Algarve seafood, regional meats, and artisan cheeses, paired with a curated selection of premium Portuguese wines from north to south.

day_by_day.notes: Purchase premium Portuguese souvenirs today — local wines, artisan ceramics, cork products, and Algarvian almond sweets make excellent gifts. Confirm departure logistics and arrange the airport transfer for the following day.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Lagos — enjoy a last leisurely gourmet breakfast at the hotel. Take a final stroll along the Lagos waterfront and marina, soaking in the atmosphere of this beautiful coastal town. Check out of the hotel and ensure all luggage is organized for departure.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure flight time, enjoy a final coffee and pastel de nata at a Lagos café, or visit any last sights missed during the trip. Private luxury transfer from Lagos to Faro Airport (~1 hour) for the return journey home.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Faro Airport. Reflect on 13 extraordinary days exploring the premium beaches, world-class wines, dramatic sea caves, and rich cultural heritage of Portugal's stunning Algarve region.

meals.breakfast: Final gourmet breakfast at Boutique Taghostel — a fitting end to a luxury stay.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a Lagos café before departure, or at the airport if time is tight.
meals.dinner: In-flight or at the destination.

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5 hours before your flight for the transfer and airport check-in. Faro Airport is approximately 60–70 minutes from Lagos. Pre-book the private luxury transfer in advance. Consider purchasing duty-free Portuguese wine and ginjinha at the airport as final souvenirs.

query: Portugal Algarve, $2200, beach holiday with wine tasting, September from London
